leftEvidence.title: The servant called Israel is sent to restore Israel

points.label: Israel setting and claim
points.left: The servant speaks from a call before birth, is named Israel, laments apparently empty labor, and receives a commission to bring Jacob back and become a light to nations.
points.right: Hosea’s children receive names announcing an end to Jehu’s house, no mercy, and not my people.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: rulers will bow because the Holy One has chosen the servant.
points.right: the oracle then speaks of innumerable children, restored peoplehood, and Judah and Israel gathered under one head.

payload.posture: Isaiah names a servant Israel who must bring Jacob back, while Hosea gives children names denying mercy and peoplehood before promising reunion.

rightEvidence.title: Children bear names of judgment and future reunion

payload.tension: Each source makes Israel both the named subject and the one needing restoration, but through different speakers, figures, and historical pressures.
payload.title: Israel named through restoration and rejected peoplehood
